doc.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024

title: Advice to young players and club dates
summary: Beal quotes Mose Allison to play every chance you get, notes fewer opportunities now, and recalls club-date work faking tunes.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: If you had — I’m going to ask you think back — in 1974 I’m going back from 2024 — what kind of advice might you have given to someone coming up as opposed to the advice you would give them now? Can we talk about what you would have said to a 19- year-old musician in 1974 trying to find a place in the business?

I guess just play — I’ll quote Mose Allison, he said, “Play every chance you get — play every chance you get.” Now there’s not as many opportunities. There’s plenty of musicians around but the opportunities are limited. All those gigs, you know, don’t pay very much. It’s hard to make a living at this time.
It’s frustrating to think why has this occurred. I guess there’s a number of reasons why some of those gigs have gone away: DJs etcetera.

Yeah. Yeah I mean I made a living playing club dates for seven years when I first got married, and now they don’t have the same — there’s no market. It’s mostly DJs I think doing that kind of work. There are some bands working at that but I don’t know, I’ve been away from that for so long. But it was — and I must say that doing that kind of work you really learn a lot you know, you learn how to fake through tunes and, you know, they used to have bands that faked everything, you know pretty big sized, like a sax section faking harmonies and you know pretty skillful players.
Oh yeah I’ve heard about that, like the band leader would say “Misty” and hold up three fingers or whatever, and then as “Misty” would come to an end they’d call another tune, two flats.
Oh yeah. The hand signals, sure. And the guys would fake harmonies and you know there was a certain pool of musicians who were excellent at that.
